_README: Solar London CLIENT FACT SHEET - TEMPLATE, awaiting Raymon.
Per AGENTS.md section 7, every client has clients/<client>/facts.json and it is the single
source of truth for names, numbers, currency, percentages, dates and codes. Every document and
email must preserve each fact verbatim.
AUTOMATED CHECK:  python scripts/verify_document.py clients/solar-london/facts.json clients/solar-london/pdfs/*.pdf
scripts/verify_document.py reads EXACTLY two keys from this file: `must_appear` and
`must_not_contain`. `must_appear` is a list of strings that must each be present in the extracted
PDF text (whitespace-normalised). `must_not_contain` is a list of strings that must each be ABSENT.
Exit code 0 = ALL PASS. Exit 1 = VERIFICATION FAILED, and the stage fails.
The extra keys in this file (business, pricing, email, quote_document, open_questions) are for
humans and agents. The script ignores them; they are here so the file is the one place a Builder
looks for a fact, rather than scattering defaults across workflow nodes.
1. Copy this file to clients/solar-london/facts.json and fill it from Raymon's written answers only.
2. Add to `must_appear` ONLY strings Raymon has actually confirmed. Do not add a price to
`must_appear` until he gives that price in writing. An unconfirmed string in `must_appear`
fails every PDF and teaches the team to pad the list.
3. Leave `must_not_contain` populated. It is the anti-hallucination guard, not filler.
4. Re-run the verification script after every quote-document change.
must_appear_note: Only one confirmed fact exists so far. Everything else is genuinely unknown, and an unknown fact must never be guessed into a PDF.
must_not_contain_note: The [YOUR_*] and YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_* entries are literal placeholders that the old quote workflow
shipped to customers. Their reappearance is a regression and must fail the stage.
'JR Marketing Agency', 'Social Media Marketing', 'CRO', 'Website Build' and 'SEO' came from the
old marketing-agency catalog. They are not Solar London services. Raymon's decision was that the
business is solar, so these are forbidden everywhere.
'TBD' is the load-bearing pricing sentinel. A delivered PDF must NEVER contain it - if it does, an
unresolved price leaked into a customer-facing document, which is the exact failure this whole
CAVEAT: the script does substring matching, not word matching. 'CRO' will also match inside any word
containing those three letters, and 'null' will match inside 'nullable'. Confirm none of these can
occur in a legitimate solar quote before relying on them, or drop the risky entry.

business.social_proof_note: The AI persona cites 'over 500+ 5 star Trustpilot reviews'. Confirm this is current and permitted on a client-facing quote before it appears on any document.
business.booking_url_note: Confirmed in the live persona prompt. A real booking link, not a placeholder - but it is a URL, not a price, and it is never to be treated as one.

persona.voice: British, casual, 30-year-old human, short messages, 2-3 sentences, occasional spelling or grammar slip, never American, never emoji, never a long dash
persona.handoff_line_literal: let me check that with my manager
persona.handoff_line_note: Taken verbatim from the live AI Conversation Agent systemMessage. In the quote sub-workflow this is a LITERAL string in the Return nodes, not model output, so it matches her voice by construction and cannot be hallucinated.

pricing.source_quote_verbatim: it depends on what the person pick it a solar panel let say it about 6k pounds
pricing.source_quote_provenance: Raymon, in conversation, 2026-09-26. This is the ONLY price datum that exists.
pricing.source_quote_note: Deliberately null. The sentence is ambiguous in at least four ways: per panel or per install; VAT-inclusive or plus VAT; a real list price or a conversational illustration; home or commercial. It is recorded as the provenance of an open question and must NEVER be parsed into a price, used as a default, or used to bound a future Raymon-supplied value.
pricing.tbd_rule: Every price-bearing catalog field is the literal string "TBD" until Raymon supplies a value in writing. Money fields are strings on purpose; the pricing Code node parses them with /^\d{1,9}(\.\d{1,2})?$/ and treats any non-match as UNRESOLVED, which ABORTS the quote.
pricing.fail_loud_rule: AGENTS.md section 9.7. An unresolved price aborts the quote and returns a pre-written human-handoff line. Never a partial quote, never a zero, never a range, never a model-invented number.
pricing.price_basis_note: Is a quote a fixed price or a site-survey estimate? This changes document wording, not just a catalog line.

email.delivery_method_note: RESOLVED DECISION. There is no Gmail credential on the instance and none is required. Delivery uses a new GoHighLevel outbound email webhook - the same mechanism already proven three times in the text agent via services.leadconnectorhq.com/hooks/... . GHL stays the single sender, the email comes from Solar London's own sending domain, and it lands in the same GHL conversation record as Amy's WhatsApp messages.
email.gmail_credential_note: null means NOT AVAILABLE and NOT ADDED. If Raymon later adds a Gmail OAuth2 credential, this is the escape hatch that would let the stock `Email the Quote` node send a native PDF attachment.
email.quote_email_webhook_url_note: BLOCKING open item. A new GHL webhook trigger gets a NEW uuid. The three existing triggers on this location are WhatsApp/SMS and must not be reused. Never guess this URL.
email.send_keyed_on_note: The send is keyed on the GHL Contact ID, not on an email string typed by a model. GHL resolves the recipient from its own contact record, so there is no path by which a hallucinated address becomes the delivery target.
email.pdf_attachment_route_note: v1 ships the quote as a styled HTML email body - zero new infrastructure, fully functional. v1.1 adds a PDF attachment via a Supabase Storage signed URL, which requires Raymon to create a bucket and to confirm `Supabase account f1` holds a SERVICE-ROLE key (anon keys cannot upload). Never a public bucket.
email.supabase_storage_policy: time-limited signed URL - never public read

quote_document.title: TBD
quote_document.title_note: Raymon's decision was that the business is solar. The old document title was a marketing-agency Service Quote and must not survive.
quote_document.subtitle: TBD
quote_document.date_format_note: Confirm with Raymon. The old document used new Date().toLocaleDateString(), which is locale-dependent and therefore not reproducible between the dev machine and production. Use an explicit format.
quote_document.table_columns_note: The old marketing columns (Monthly Price / One-Time Price) do not fit a solar quote and must not be carried over. Confirm the final column set with Raymon.
quote_document.terms_line_note: e.g. prices subject to a site survey. If the quote is an estimate rather than a fixed price, this line is not optional.
quote_document.chat_format: plain text, no markdown, no bullets, no bold, no tables, no HTML, each price in its own message
quote_document.chat_format_note: Matches the live persona's existing output rules so the quote reads like the rest of Amy's messages.

kpi_note: Solar London has no confirmed dashboard deployment, so no dashboard KPI facts are recorded here. If a dashboard is later deployed, the quote sub-workflow may post an optional `quote_generated` event with the canonical envelope { event_type, client_id, timestamp, payload } per AGENTS.md section 7.1. `quote_generated` is additive and does not replace conversation_started, booking_made, handed_off_to_human, or follow_up_triggered. A `quote_generated` KPI card is NOT in scope for the first build.
open_questions: See clients/solar-london/build-spec/quote-integration-spec.md section 17. Twenty-eight questions: ten about pricing, four about the catalog, six about business facts, six build-blocking technical questions, two that can safely be defaulted.
verification_stage_gate: Roadmap stage S1 cannot complete until this command prints ALL PASS on at least one real rendered quote PDF.
